hypothesis: A shared timing error evolves slowly into periodic blanking, or rapidly into a transport fault/restart. Its derivative influences the time to failure.

counterexamples.limit: No report does not establish zero physical timing error.
Sparse unchanged-value logging cannot establish instantaneous derivative.
Measured elapsed DSP duration does not separate CPU time from descheduling; a timing common cause remains possible.

measurement_limits: Private ioDriftNS field has no verified public definition; not a direct physical clock-error measurement.
Many records are ~2ms steps associated with zero-length transfer reports, rather than a smooth drift measurement.
Segment by IO restart/transfer-manager epoch before finite differencing.
A USB transaction error precedes the observed restart; numerical drift must explain that transport failure, not just the recovery.
Periodic improvement while drift continues rising requires phase/alignment or recovery state, not monotonically increasing damage.
current_experiment_prediction: After archive retrieval, compare drift increments/slopes, zero-length transfers and USB faults across verified nominal/inducedSerious/off phases. Determine whether drift changes precede the symptom change; retain missing logging and unavailable reversal limitations.
